Most state highway agencies consider a 10-year frequency storm as the minimum for design of storm drains. Storm drains in sag locations are typically checked for the 50-year frequency storm.
When gaged data are not available, estimates are made by empirical equations (e.g., Rational Method) or by regional regression equations.
When gaged data of adequate length and quality are available, statistical analysis of the flow record can be used to estimate flood peaks for various return periods.
Point rainfall data are used to derive intensity-duration-frequency curves necessary in hydrologic analysis (e.g., as required in the Rational Method; see Section 2.5).
The resulting set of equations, referred to as the USGS rural regression equations, were developed primarily for unregulated, natural, nonurbanized watersheds.
To estimate peak discharge in urban areas, equations were developed that modify the rural peak discharge computed as described above.
the USGS compiled all statewide and metropolitan area regression equations into a computer program titled the National Streamflow Statistics (NSS) program.
